proposed_widenings.name: resource-less_magic_item_activation
proposed_widenings.justification: The closest family is magic-item activation, but the current activation header requires a consumable resource and reset cadence. Eversmoking Bottle is a reusable open-or-close toggle with no charge pool or use counter.
proposed_widenings.evidence: As a Magic action, you can open or close this bottle.

proposed_widenings.name: manual_toggle_duration_for_item_effects
proposed_widenings.justification: The smoke persists while the bottle stays open, with no fixed maximum duration, then changes behavior when the bottle is closed. Existing Duration variants do not express item-owned persistence that lasts until the user toggles it off.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Each minute the bottle remains open, the size of the Emanation increases by 10 feet until it reaches its maximum size of 120 feet.

proposed_widenings.name: area_origin_on_item_object
proposed_widenings.justification: The smoke emanates from the bottle itself, not from self, a target, or a point-within-range chosen at activation time. Existing area origins do not represent an item/object as the anchor.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Opening the bottle causes thick smoke to billow out, forming a cloud that fills a 60-foot Emanation originating from the bottle.

proposed_widenings.name: expanding_area_then_lingering_fixed_cloud
proposed_widenings.justification: The area grows by timed increments while open, then becomes a fixed lingering cloud on close with a separate dispersal timer. That is a stateful area-life-cycle transition, not a single existing attachment or duration shape.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Closing the bottle causes the cloud to become fixed in place until it disperses after 10 minutes.

notes: No content file was authored. The closest fit is a magic-item activation, but the current surface cannot express a reusable toggleable object-centered area that expands over elapsed minutes and then lingers after closing. Per local precedent in content/cloudkill.dhall, 'Heavily Obscured' is caller-owned visibility and strong-wind dispersal is caller-resolved, so this is classified as surface_widening rather than atom_widening.
